seo_title: Cost of Living in Seville 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Seville per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: The capital of Andalusia in southern Spain: a hot climate, flamenco, Moorish architecture and an unhurried southern pace. Cheaper than Madrid and Barcelona; Russian citizens need a visa, and summers are scorching.
pros: A hot climate and a long warm season
cons: Very scorching summers (up to +40 and above)
No sea in the city (you have to travel to the coast)

visa_steps.title: Schengen visa
visa_steps.description: Russian citizens need a Schengen or national visa — Spain is part of the Schengen area.

visa_steps.title: NIE
visa_steps.description: A foreigner's identification number — required for almost all procedures.

visa_steps.title: Registration (empadronamiento)
visa_steps.description: Registration at your place of residence with the city hall.

visa_steps.title: Bank account
visa_steps.description: Spanish banks open accounts once you have an NIE and an address.

visa_steps.title: Residence permit (TIE)
visa_steps.description: A resident card is issued after entry on a long-term visa (for example, a nomad visa).

faq.question: Do Russian citizens need a visa for Seville?
faq.answer: Yes, you need a Schengen or national visa — Spain is part of the Schengen area.

faq.question: How much does it cost to live in Seville?
faq.answer: Cheaper than Madrid and Barcelona. See the exact budget in the calculator above.

faq.question: What language is spoken in Seville?
faq.answer: Spanish (with an Andalusian accent); there's little English.

faq.question: Can I pay with a Russian card in Seville?
faq.answer: No, Russian cards don't work. You'll need a card from a foreign bank or euros in cash.

faq.question: What is the climate like in Seville?
faq.answer: Hot Mediterranean: very scorching summers and mild winters — one of the warmest cities in Europe.

faq.question: Is Seville suitable for remote work?
faq.answer: Yes, with Spain's nomad visa; it's valued for its climate, culture and affordability relative to the major cities.

reviews.text: Seville is sun, flamenco and an unhurried pace, cheaper than Madrid. The downsides are the brutal summer heat and the Schengen for entry, and there's no sea in the city.
Southern colour, beautiful architecture, a warm winter. Living is pleasant and not too expensive by Spanish standards. The main challenge is the visa and Spanish.
